A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LEN/LEN-restart work. Sections 1-6 and Appendices A-G can be matched; v2 adds Appendix H. The text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1-2 report original optimization experiments on synthetic regularized bilinear problems and fairness-aware learning using heart, adult, and law school data.

after.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1-2 report original results on the same tasks, including separate synthetic convergence curves for multiple Hessian-reuse intervals.

M1.justification: The original LEN and LEN-restart procedures remain, but Appendix H adds an inexact LEN variant with a multiplicative acceptance condition (Algorithm 4) and an explicit bracketing/log-scale bisection solver (Algorithm 5). These introduce a substantive alternative to requiring an exact cubic subproblem solution.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic cubic-regularized bilinear task and fairness-aware learning on heart, adult, and law school. Changes to synthetic dimensions and reuse intervals concern settings within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The empirical comparators remain EG and the second-order method obtained with m = 1. The latter is called EG-2 in v1 and NPE in v2. Newly discussed QNPE is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes synthetic sizes from n = {100, 200, 500} to {10, 100, 200}, replaces tuning m over {10, 100, d} with reporting {1, 2, 10, 100}, and removes distance-to-saddle evaluation from Figure 1. The real-data settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 1 adds an explicit sensitivity comparison of Hessian-reuse intervals through LEN-2, LEN-10, and LEN-100. V1 reports only a selected LEN curve after tuning m, so it does not expose this sensitivity.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments.

E6.justification: The synthetic result set in Figure 1 is substantially revised: v2 adds n = 10 and separate reuse-interval trajectories, while removing n = 500 and all distance-to-saddle trajectories. The broad runtime advantage remains, but the revised result set does not establish a same-setting performance improvement over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix H adds inexact convergence and subproblem-complexity theorems with supporting lemmas, and Appendices C-D generalize the analysis accordingly. A new restricted-gap lemma supports revised reasoning and changes Theorem 4.1's constant from 9 to 32. Definitions 3.3 and 3.5 and the induction arithmetic in Appendix B are also corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: lazy Hessian reuse improves total computational complexity by a factor of d^(1/3), with LEN for convex-concave problems and LEN-restart for strongly-convex-strongly-concave problems.

C2.justification: Appendix H explicitly acknowledges that the exact cubic subproblem solution assumed previously cannot be obtained in practice and explains the need for an inexact treatment. Section 4.3 also discusses the new solver analysis's applicability without a positive lower bound on the Jacobian's smallest singular value.

D1.justification: V2 adds a source-code repository link in Section 5 and specifies the inexact solver's initialization, acceptance interval, and termination procedure. The reported processor and real-data hyperparameter settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 explicitly positions LEN within the NPE lineage, adds discussion of Jiang et al.'s QNPE, and connects the already-cited C2EDEN work to lazy updates. It adds Rockafellar and Williams et al. references and removes the control-theoretic and high-order reduced-gradient references, while retaining the overall research framing.

P1.justification: V2 revises introductory and technical explanations, standardizes the NPE terminology, moves the notation paragraph, and adds acknowledgments and conference information. The main section sequence and much of the narrative remain intact; the new appendix primarily adds scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 adopts conference typography, margins, headers, and author layout. Figure 1 changes from six panels to three with additional curves; Figure 2 is redisplayed with revised axes and markers. Table 1 drops separate C-C EG-2 and Perseus rows, and two algorithm displays are added.

improvement.justification: V2 improves implementation clarity and theoretical checkability through the inexact solver, expanded analysis, corrected restricted-gap reasoning, and code-access information. The reuse-interval study adds useful evidence, but replaces the larger synthetic case and distance plots. The new analysis also remains internally inconsistent: Appendix D derives a 32α gap constant, whereas Theorems H.1-H.2 state 16α. These unresolved details limit the strength of the overall improvement.
